content:
# VitaDeck

VitaDeck runs React-authored **Deck Apps** on a PlayStation Vita. A C host (raylib + QuickJS) renders an instance tree that a custom React reconciler drives; the same host builds for macOS/Linux for development. `@vitadeck/sdk` on npm is how Deck App authors build and package apps.

Prefer simple systems and small diffs. Fight scope creep; honor the dev's intent minimally. Leave the repo buildable after every change.

## Glossary

Read [CONTEXT.md](./CONTEXT.md) before naming anything user-facing or Shell-facing. It is the ubiquitous language (Deck App, Deck App Package, VitaDeck Shell, Runtime Upload, System Input, ...) and lists the words to avoid. `docs/adr/` holds the decisions behind the native layout; read the ones that touch your area and flag it loudly if your change contradicts one.

When this file speaks:

- `you` is the agent reading this file and changing VitaDeck.
- `author` is a developer building a Deck App with the SDK, outside this repo.
- `host` is the desktop build of the native app; `Vita` is the device build.

## How it works

`pnpm --dir js build` compiles the SDK, the example Deck Apps (`js/examples/*/dist/*.vdapp`), and the runtime bundle (`js/dist/runtime/runtime.js`). The host CMake build reruns that when files under `js/` change and links `js/dist/runtime` and `assets/` into the build tree; the `stage_examples` target (also run by `run`) copies the examples into `<build>/vitadeck-data/installed-deck-apps`, a plain `cmake --build out` does not. The everyday loop is `ninja -C out run`. At startup `src/core/bootstrap.c` inits raylib, fonts, and the QuickJS runtime, loads the **Active Deck App** from the **Installed Deck App Library**, and the reconciler in `js/packages/runtime` mutates the native instance tree that `src/ui/render.c` paints each frame. `Start`/F1 toggles the **VitaDeck Shell**, and VitaDeck runs the **LAN Listener** (HTTP on 8787, from startup) for **Runtime Upload** of `.vdapp.zip` archives and **Host Control Links**.

## Where code lives

- `src/core/` - bootstrap, QuickJS runtime, event queue, package library and manifest parsing (vendored `vendor/jimp/jimp.h` behind `json.c`, see ADR 0003), Benchmark Mode (`bench.c`, see ADR 0005)
- `src/jslib/` - native functions exposed to JS: instances, timers, fetch, log, colors
- `src/ui/` - instance tree, rendering, fonts, images, input, scroll
- `src/shell/` - VitaDeck Shell; `src/net/` - the LAN Listener (Runtime Upload and Host Control Link) and HTTP request parsing; `src/upload/` - archive extraction; `src/host_control/` - link parsing and store; `src/platform/` - threads and LAN address (POSIX vs Vita)
- `js/packages/sdk/` - `@vitadeck/sdk`: author-facing components, theme, types, and the `vitadeck` CLI (`cli/`, scaffold under `cli/templates/`)
- `js/packages/runtime/` - the React reconciler bundle the host embeds
- `js/packages/host-companion/` - the Host Companion (`vitadeck-host-companion`, unpublished) with the built-in Host Control Plugins; a custom plugin is a `.vdplugin` package the SDK CLI builds (`hostPlugin` in `vitadeck.config.json`, scaffolded with a Deck App by `create --host-plugin` or alone by `create --host-plugin-only`). The wire contract is `js/packages/sdk/src/host-control/` and the fixtures in `tests/fixtures/host-control/`, replayed by the SDK, companion and native tests (ADR 0004)
- `js/examples/` - example Deck Apps; the smoke test screenshots every section of `demo`
- `tests/` - CTest harnesses (`smoke_harness.c`, `deck_app_input_harness.c`, `package_manifest_harness.c`, `package_library_harness.c`, `timer_reload_harness.c`, `upload_parsing_harness.c`, `host_control_link_harness.c`), golden screenshots (`fixtures/golden/`), and benchmark baselines (`bench/baselines/`)
- `vendor/quickjs` - git submodule; `docker-compose.yml` + `Dockerfile` - Vitasdk and Linux smoke images
- `.agents/skills/` - repo skills (`vitadeck-build`, `vitadeck-emulator`, `vitadeck-smoke`, `vitadeck-bench`, `vitadeck-manual-testing`, `vitadeck-vdapp-upload`, `vitadeck-deck-app-init`, `vitadeck-host-control`) plus `comprehende` installed from `matemolnar8/comprehende` via the `skills` CLI (`skills-lock.json`) and `pages`, a repo-owned skill with its own publish script. `.claude/skills` symlinks here. Published via `npx skills add matemolnar8/vitadeck`.

## Setup

- Node.js 24.16+ (`.nvmrc`; `fnm use` picks it up, and `scripts/agent-check.sh` switches to it through fnm on its own) and pnpm (pinned by `packageManager` in `js/package.json`). `pnpm --dir js install` once. Older Node bundles a corepack that cannot launch pnpm 11+ and fails with `Cannot find module .../bin/pnpm.cjs`.
- `git submodule update --init --recursive` if `vendor/quickjs/quickjs.c` is missing.
- Host build needs CMake, Ninja, raylib 5.5, curl, OpenSSL, zlib (`brew install ninja raylib` on macOS; Ninja, raylib + OpenGL/X11 dev packages on Linux). Configure `out/` with `cmake --preset default`. A build directory keeps the generator it was configured with; delete an old Make `out/` before configuring it with a preset.
- Vita build and Linux smoke run in Docker. Start Docker Desktop first.
- The first CMake configure downloads the pinned runtime fonts and Twemoji images ([cmake/fonts.cmake](cmake/fonts.cmake), [cmake/twemoji.cmake](cmake/twemoji.cmake)) into the gitignored `assets/fonts/` and `assets/emoji/`; offline it warns, builds anyway with fallbacks (raylib's built-in font, missing-glyph boxes for CJK and Korean, a fallback glyph for emoji), and the next configure retries.
- Uploading a Vita build (`upload_vita`, `upload_vpk`, `run`) reads the Vita's IP from `PSVITAIP` when CMake configures, e.g. `export PSVITAIP=192.168.1.177`.
- Without the device, `scripts/vita3k.sh` builds the VPK and runs it in the [Vita3K](https://vita3k.org) emulator (macOS, Windows via Git Bash, Linux) with the example Deck Apps installed. New machine setup (Vita3K, Sony's shader compiler) and controls: [the `vitadeck-emulator` skill](.agents/skills/vitadeck-emulator/SKILL.md). Start is Enter in Vita3K, not F1.
- Releases: [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md).

## Footguns

1. **Stale `js/dist`.** The host CMake build reruns `pnpm build` when JS changes; the Vita build packs `js/dist` as it finds it. After any change under `js/`, run `pnpm --dir js build` before a Vita build, or you will debug yesterday's JS on the Vita.
2. **Two-language package format.** The Deck App Package Manifest is validated natively in `src/core/package_manifest.c` and produced by the SDK CLI. A change to one without the other ships packages the host rejects, or accepts packages the SDK never emits. Update both and the `package_manifest` CTest harness.
3. **Platform goldens.** `tests/fixtures/golden/Linux/` holds the only canonical goldens (ADR 0002). Refresh it only with `scripts/smoke-docker.sh update-golden`, never from a macOS run. Do not re-enable the `smoke` CTest label in the macOS ctest step.
4. **Secrets in examples.** `js/examples/chat/src/genesys/genesys.local.ts` is gitignored and holds real credentials. Never commit it, never paste its contents, and never "fix" imports by renaming it.
5. **Running from the wrong cwd.** The host resolves `vitadeck-data/` relative to the working directory (or `VITADECK_DATA_ROOT`). Run `./vitadeck` from `out/`, not the repo root.

## Hit every surface

The common defect is a change that works on the host and breaks the Vita, or works in one example and breaks the SDK contract.

- **Targets.** Host (macOS/Linux) and Vita share `src/`. Anything touching threads, filesystem, networking, or GL belongs behind `src/platform/` or needs a Vita Docker build to prove it.
- **Author contract.** `@vitadeck/sdk` is published. A change to its exports, types, CLI flags, scaffold template, or manifest shape is a breaking change for authors. Bump the Deck App Package Schema Version when the manifest shape changes.
- **Inputs.** Vita buttons and host keyboard mappings (F1 Start, Enter confirm, Backspace back) must stay in sync in `src/ui/input.c` and in `CONTEXT.md`.
- **Reverse states.** Upload needs cancel, install needs removal, Shell open needs Shell close. Check the failure paint, not just success.
- **Docs.** If a change makes `CONTEXT.md`, an ADR, the SDK README, or a skill inaccurate, fix it in place. Do not append a second account.

## Verifying

Use `scripts/agent-check.sh` from the repo root; pick the smallest tier that proves the change:

- `fast` - JS install and build, JS typecheck, SDK CLI tests, Host Companion tests, JS lint, JS and C format checks. Run after every change.
- `host` - JS install and build, host build, non-smoke CTest. Run for any `src/` or runtime change.
- `smoke` - Dockerized Linux visual smoke and Deck App input check. Run when rendering, theme, fonts, input, or Deck App output change.
- `full` - all of the above plus the Vita Docker build. Run before a PR that touches native code.

Individual commands: `pnpm --dir js tsc`, `pnpm --dir js test:cli`, `pnpm --dir js test:host-companion`, `pnpm --dir js lint`, `pnpm --dir js format:check`, `pnpm --dir js build`, `./scripts/clang-format.sh check` (or `format` to apply), `cmake --preset default && cmake --build out`, Vita: `docker compose run --rm vitasdk bash -lc "cmake -S . -B out-vita && cmake --build out-vita"`.

- C under `src/` and `tests/` follows `.clang-format` with clang-format 21 (CI pins 21.1.8, `pipx install clang-format==21.1.8`); run `cmake --preset default` so `out/compile_commands.json` exists for clangd.
- Write React for the React Compiler: pure renders, Rules of Hooks, accurate effect deps, no manual `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`memo`.
- For a change that could affect performance (rendering, the reconciler, the JS thread loop), run `scripts/bench.sh vita3k` and compare against the baseline; see the `vitadeck-bench` skill.
- For a UI change, do one pass in the real host window (load the `vitadeck-manual-testing` skill). Ask before testing on Vita hardware; it is Máté's device.

## Pull requests

- Open a PR only when asked, or when requested feature work is ready under an approved plan.
- Conventional titles, plain language: `fix(shell): upload screen shows bind failure`.
- Body: the problem in a sentence or two, then how you fixed it, then which agent-check tier passed.
- Review the diff with the `comprehende` skill (base is the merge-base with `main`, head is the branch tip), `export` it, then host the export with the `pages` skill using `--pr <number>`. Put the printed URL in the PR body. When the PR gets new commits, refresh the review and publish again to the same URL.
- UI changes need before/after screenshots or an updated golden. Upload evidence to GitHub; do not commit PR-only images.
- One request is one PR.

## Documentation

Most code changes do not need a docs change. Agents can read the code.

- `README.md` and `js/packages/sdk/README.md` are for authors. Change them when a CLI command, install step, or author-visible behavior changes.
- `CONTEXT.md` is the glossary. Add a term only when a new user-facing concept appears; keep the "Avoid" lines current.
- `docs/adr/` is for decisions and their reasons. One file per decision, rewrite when it changes, never append a second account.
- Do not enumerate fields, narrate control flow, or keep file catalogs. Link to source instead.

## Plans and work artifacts

- Do not commit plans, research notes, or scratch files. Keep them outside the worktree.
- GitHub Issues on `matemolnar8/vitadeck` are the tracker; use `gh`. A merged PR is the implementation record.

## Notes from Máté

I want simple C and simple TypeScript solving a real problem: React on a PS Vita. The host is a thin, honest rendering of the instance tree, and the SDK is the only public surface. Keep platform quirks behind `src/platform/`, keep the manifest contract explicit, and prefer deleting machinery over adding it.
